blocks.task_summary: Find the exact value of E(X) where X has PDF f(x)=6/(π√(16-x²)) for 0≤x≤2.
method_path: Integrate by substitution u=16-x² or x=4sinθ
Obtain antiderivative expression with correct constants
Simplify to exact value (12/π)(2-√3) or equivalent

evidence.basis: E(X)=∫₀² x·6/(π√(16-x²))dx (A1); attempt to integrate using inspection/substitution (M1); integrated expression e.g. (6/2π)(-2√(16-x²)) (A1); attempt to substitute limits and evaluate (M1); final answer (A1). Note accepts (24/π)(1-cos(π/6)) for final A1.

blocks.task_summary: Find P(X<0.5) for the given continuous PDF.
method_path: Evaluate integral using GDC to obtain 0.239

blocks.task_summary: Determine the least number of independent trials required to be 99% sure of at least one success, where success is defined as X<0.5.
method_path: Recognise P(at least one success)=1−P(no successes)=1−(1−p)^n
accepted_alternatives: Recognise Y~B(n, 0.239…), test n=16 (P≈0.987…) and n=17 (P≈0.990…), select n=17

evidence.basis: EITHER: recognition P(at least one success)=1−P(no successes) (M1); 1−(1−0.239…)^n ≥ 0.99 (A1); n=16.8321… so 17 trials (A1). OR: recognition Y~B(n,0.239…) (M1); n=16 gives 0.987443… and n=17 gives 0.990448… (A1); 17 trials (A1).

blocks.task_summary: For ten independent trials, find the probability that exactly three trials are successful.

evidence.basis: Recognition that Y~B(10, their part b) (M1); P(X=3)=0.242430… ≈ 0.242 (A1).

blocks.task_summary: Write down the number of ways three successful trials could have occurred consecutively in ten trials.
method_path: Count starting positions for a block of 3 consecutive successes in 10 trials: positions 1–3 through 8–10

blocks.task_summary: (i) Write an expression for the number of ways three successful trials could occur consecutively in n trials. (ii) Find the greatest n such that the probability of three consecutive successes is more than 0.05.
method_path: (i) Express number of ways as n−2
(ii) Express total ways to choose 3 successes from n as C(n,3)
Form probability as (n−2)/C(n,3) and simplify to 6/(n(n−1))
accepted_alternatives: Solve (n−2)/C(n,3) > 0.05 directly; use table of values for n=11 and n=12

evidence.basis: (i) n−2 (A1). (ii) C(n,3) (A1); (n−2)/C(n,3) (A1); attempt to solve their expression > 0.05 OR 6/(n(n−1)) > 0.05 (M1); n=11 gives 0.0545454… and n=12 gives 0.0454545… (A1); n=11 (A1).
